_comment: Read aloud (wheel button F14). The first engine whose programs and files all exist is used. A stage is one program and its arguments; the text is written to the first stage's stdin and each stage's output goes to the next one's stdin. Arguments are used exactly as written: nothing is substituted, and the spoken text is never in an argument or a shell.

engines.name: piper
engines._comment: FROM MEMORY AND UNTESTED: these Piper options and the raw 22050 Hz output are not checked against a real Piper. The paths are where pi/README.md, section Piper, puts the program and the voice (documented steps, no script installs it; still from memory and untested).

engines.name: espeak-ng
engines._comment: Fallback. espeak-ng reads the text from stdin when it gets no text argument.
